clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old male presented with worsening chronic lower back and right lower extremity pain and numbness. Lumbar spine MRI revealed a suspicious metastatic lesion in the L3 vertebral body and moderate to severe left hydroureteronephrosis. Subsequent CT abdomen and pelvis identified an irregular soft tissue mass at the left posterolateral bladder base, highly suggestive of neoplasm, and numerous lytic bone lesions consistent with metastatic disease. A CT head showed no intracranial metastasis. Biopsy results confirmed metastatic carcinoma, consistent with urothelial carcinoma (UC).
